name: A3144
description: Temperature-stable, sensitive unipolar Hall-effect switch in a 3-pin TO-92 (SIP-3). It outputs a digital (on/off) signal, not a linear field measurement: the open-collector output pulls low when south-pole flux exceeds the operate point and releases when it falls below the release point. It integrates a voltage regulator, Hall element, Schmitt-trigger comparator and open-collector NPN output, operating from 4.5 to 24 V. Widely used for proximity, position and RPM sensing.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: supply voltage 4.5-24 V (branded/marked face toward you, leftmost pin)

pins.name: OUTPUT
pins.description: open-collector NPN output, active-low, needs external pull-up (rightmost pin)

extra.output: open-collector NPN, sink up to 25 mA
extra.temperature_stability: internal regulator for stable operation over temperature

typical_application: Magnetic proximity/limit switch, brushless motor commutation, RPM and tachometer pickups, door/lid open detection, flow-meter pulse counting.
gotchas: the output is open-collector and active-low: it REQUIRES an external pull-up resistor (commonly 10k) to read a logic high
it is a digital SWITCH (unipolar, on/off), not a linear/ratiometric field sensor - do not expect an analog field reading like an A1302/A1308
unipolar and south-pole sensitive: only one magnet polarity facing the branded face triggers it; the wrong pole or wrong face never switches
verify TO-92 pin order with the BRANDED face toward you, leads down: pin1=VCC, pin2=GND, pin3=OUTPUT - reversing VCC and OUTPUT can damage the part
no built-in reverse-polarity protection; swapping VCC/GND can destroy it - add a series resistor or diode if supply polarity is uncertain
the original A3141-4 series is obsolete; most parts sold today are A3144E/OH3144 clones with the same pinout and behavior
